```{python}
def barh(series, title, xlabel, color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=False, figsize=(7.2, 4.4)):
    s = series.sort_values(ascending=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.barh(s.index, s.values, color=color)
    total = s.sum()
    for y, v in enumerate(s.values):
        lbl = f"{v:,} ({v/total*100:.0f}%)" if fmt_pct else f"{v:,}"
        ax.text(v, y, " " + lbl, va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel); ax.set_title(title)
    ax.margins(x=0.16); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: load-comparison
CMP = pd.ExcelFile(CMP_FILE)
cmp_summary = CMP.parse("Сводка")
SUMMARY = dict(zip(cmp_summary["Показатель"], cmp_summary["Значение"]))

doc1 = CMP.parse("Документ 1 с результатом")     # 2022 stage, 3 okrugs
matches = CMP.parse("Совпадения")
probable = CMP.parse("Вероятные совпадения")
only1 = CMP.parse("Только в документе 1")
only2 = CMP.parse("Только в документе 2")
gps_warn = CMP.parse("GPS-предупреждения")

# ---- Reconstruct document 2 (the new 3-okrug export) --------------------
# The workbook never ships document 2 as a sheet of its own; every one of its
# rows appears exactly once across the three result sheets, carrying the full
# "Документ 2: *" column block. Concatenating them and de-duplicating on the
# document-2 row number rebuilds the export verbatim.
D2_COLS = [c for c in matches.columns if c.startswith("Документ 2: ")]
v2 = (pd.concat([df[["Строка в документе 2"] + D2_COLS]
                 for df in (matches, probable, only2)], ignore_index=True)
        .drop_duplicates(subset="Строка в документе 2")
        .sort_values("Строка в документе 2")
        .reset_index(drop=True))
v2.columns = [c.replace("Документ 2: ", "") for c in v2.columns]
v2 = v2.rename(columns=V2_RENAME)

for col in ("latitude", "longitude", "provider_count"):
    v2[col] = pd.to_numeric(v2[col], errors="coerce")
v2["category_en"] = v2["category_orig"].map(CATEGORY_EN).fillna(v2["category_orig"])
v2["district_en"] = v2["district_orig"].map(DISTRICT_EN).fillna(v2["district_orig"])

n_v2 = len(v2)
n_declared = int(SUMMARY["Строк в документе 2"])
n_doc1 = int(SUMMARY["Строк в документе 1"])
n_match = int(SUMMARY["Найдено совпадений"])
n_prob = int(SUMMARY["Вероятных совпадений"])
n_only1 = int(SUMMARY["Только в документе 1"])
n_only2 = int(SUMMARY["Только в документе 2"])
tol_m = SUMMARY["Допуск сравнения, м"]
name_thr = SUMMARY["Порог похожести названий"]
```

```{python}
# | label: recode-2022
# Identical rules to analysis/v1/eda.qmd, so the two reports stay comparable.
CLASS_2022 = ["Medical", "Sport", "Grocery shops", "Catering",
              "Alcohol shops", "Tobacco outlets", "Industrial"]
ORDER_2022 = CLASS_2022 + ["Other (outside 2022 scheme)"]
OTHER = "Other (outside 2022 scheme)"
SRC2022_EN = {
    "Медицинские организации": "Medical", "Спортивные объекты": "Sport",
    "Магазины": "Grocery shops", "Общепит": "Catering",
    "Спецмагазины алкоголя": "Alcohol shops", "Точки продажи табака": "Tobacco outlets",
    "Пром. Объекты": "Industrial",
}
GROCERY_TYPES = {
    "продуктовый магазин", "супермаркет", "гипермаркет", "овощи и фрукты",
    "фрукты-овощи", "булочная", "кулинария", "ярмарка", "рынок",
    "магазин: confectionery", "кондитерская", "мясной магазин",
    "рыбный магазин", "молочный магазин", "магазин у дома",
}


def _has(s, *words):
    m = np.zeros(len(s), dtype=bool)
    for w in words:
        m |= s.str.contains(w, regex=False, na=False)
    return m


def recode_2022(df):
    """Map objects onto the 2022 taxonomy using category + type + name."""
    cat = df["category_orig"].fillna("").astype(str)
    t = df["type_orig"].fillna("").astype(str).str.lower()
    blob = (cat.str.lower() + " | " + t + " | "
            + df["name_orig"].fillna("").astype(str).str.lower())

    tobacco = (cat == "Точки продажи табака") | _has(blob, "табак", "вейп", "сигарет", "кальян", "vape")
    alcohol = _has(t, "алкогол") | _has(blob, "алкомаркет", "винотек") | (_has(t, "винный") & _has(t, "магазин"))
    medical = (cat == "Медицинские организации") | _has(
        blob, "аптек", "поликлин", "больниц", "стоматолог", "клиник", "врач",
        "диагност", "лаборатор", "диспансер", "госпит", "медиц", "оптика",
        "реабилит", "санатор", "профилакт", "роддом", "родильн", "фельдшер")
    sport = (cat == "Спортивные объекты") | _has(
        blob, "спорт", "фитнес", "бассейн", "стадион", "тренаж", "воркаут",
        "каток", "манеж", "йога") | _has(t, "парк", "сквер", "набережн")
    catering = cat.isin(["Общепит", "фастфуд"]) | _has(
        t, "кафе", "фастфуд", "бар", "ресторан", "паб", "кофейн", "столов",
        "закусочн", "пиццери", "суши", "бистро")
    grocery = t.isin(GROCERY_TYPES)
    industrial = _has(blob, "завод", "энергокомплекс", "тэц", "гэс", "фабрика", "промышл", "комбинат")

    return pd.Series(np.select(
        [tobacco, alcohol, medical, sport, catering, grocery, industrial],
        ["Tobacco outlets", "Alcohol shops", "Medical", "Sport", "Catering",
         "Grocery shops", "Industrial"], default=OTHER), index=df.index)


v2["category_2022"] = recode_2022(v2)
in_scheme = int((v2["category_2022"] != OTHER).sum())
```

# Introduction

This report is the **exploratory data analysis of the second data delivery**
(`data/raw_v2/`, 2026-08-24) of the Northern State Medical University
infrastructure project. It follows the first-delivery report
(`reports/v1/eda.pdf` / `analysis/v1/eda.qmd`) and keeps the same research
question: **how health-relevant urban infrastructure and health risk factors are
distributed across the okrugs of Arkhangelsk.**

Unlike the first delivery — a single city-wide object export — this one contains
**three different artefacts**:

1. **Comparison workbook** — `сравнение_документов_2026-08-24_093901.xlsx`.
   A record-level comparison of the **2022 stage document**
   (`{python} f"{n_doc1:,}"` rows) against a **new 2026 export restricted to the
   three 2022 okrugs** (`{python} f"{n_declared:,}"` rows).
2. **Comparison summary** — `итоги_сравнения_3_округа.csv`.
   The per-okrug summary of that comparison.
3. **Indicator panel** — `ARKTMED_Arkhangelsk_2021-2026_all_categories_...xlsx`.
   A **municipal indicator panel** for Arkhangelsk, 2021-2026, plus a composite
   risk index.

The report is organised accordingly: @sec-export analyses the new export,
@sec-comparison the 2022↔2026 comparison, and @sec-arktmed the indicator panel.

::: {.callout-important}
## The headline of this delivery
The **okrug-assignment defect** documented in the first report — where ~71% of
all objects fell into a single okrug — **is fixed in the new export.** District
attribution is now plausible and agrees with the 2022 stage on 100% of matched
records (@sec-okrug, @sec-okrug-agreement). The cost is a **loss of source
diversity**: the new export is 100% OpenStreetMap, with the 2GIS provider absent
(@sec-verification).
:::

# Part I — the corrected 3-okrug export {#sec-export}

## How the export was recovered

The comparison workbook does not ship document 2 as a sheet of its own. However,
each of its `{python} f"{n_declared:,}"` rows appears exactly once across the
sheets *Совпадения*, *Вероятные совпадения* and *Только в документе 2*, always
with the full `Документ 2: *` column block. Concatenating those blocks and
de-duplicating on the document-2 row number **reconstructs the export verbatim**
— `{python} f"{n_v2:,}"` unique rows, matching the declared
`{python} f"{n_declared:,}"`. All of Part I is computed on that reconstruction.


first export's okrug labels were unreliable, so the difference is not a real
change in the city (see @sec-okrug).

## Source verification: a regression {#sec-verification}

```{python}
# | label: fig-verification
# | fig-cap: "Source provenance, new export vs. the first export restricted to the same three okrugs."
VERIF_EN = {"only_osm": "OSM only", "only_2gis": "2GIS only",
            "confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm": "OSM + 2GIS (confirmed)"}
labels = ["OSM only", "2GIS only", "OSM + 2GIS (confirmed)"]
v1c = v1_3["verification_status"].map(VERIF_EN).value_counts().reindex(labels).fillna(0)
v2c = v2["verification_status"].map({"Только OSM": "OSM only"}).value_counts().reindex(labels).fillna(0)

y = np.arange(len(labels)); h = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 2.9))
ax.barh(y + h/2, v1c.values, h, color=OLD, label=f"v1, 3 okrugs (n={n_v1_3:,})")
ax.barh(y - h/2, v2c.values, h, color=ACCENT, label=f"v2 export (n={n_v2:,})")
for yy, v in zip(y + h/2, v1c.values):
    ax.text(v, yy, f" {int(v):,}", va="center", fontsize=8)
for yy, v in zip(y - h/2, v2c.values):
    ax.text(v, yy, f" {int(v):,}", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(labels)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects"); ax.set_title("Source provenance")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.margins(x=0.18)
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Every object in the new export carries `Статус проверки = Только OSM`,
`Источники = OSM`, `Количество источников = 1`, and every match identifier is an
`osm:node/way/relation` reference. **The 2GIS provider has disappeared
entirely.** In the same three okrugs the first export still contained
`{python} f"{int((v1_3['verification_status'] == 'only_2gis').sum()):,}"`
2GIS-only and
`{python} f"{int((v1_3['verification_status'] == 'confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm').sum()):,}"`
cross-confirmed objects; both groups are gone. This is the most likely reason
the object count fell from `{python} f"{n_v1_3:,}"` to
`{python} f"{n_v2:,}"`, and it means **no object in this delivery is
independently corroborated.** Counts remain lower bounds, and the multi-source
enrichment step of the 2022 methodology needs to be restored before the export
is treated as an inventory.

## Field completeness

```{python}
# | label: fig-completeness
# | fig-cap: "Attribute completeness, new export vs. the first export in the same three okrugs."
fields = {"Address": "adress_orig", "Opening hours": "opening_hours_orig",
          "Phone": "phone_orig", "Website": "website_orig",
          "Opening date": "opening_date_orig"}
c2 = pd.Series({k: v2[c].notna().mean()*100 for k, c in fields.items()})
c1 = pd.Series({k: v1_3[c].notna().mean()*100 for k, c in fields.items()})
c2 = c2.sort_values(); c1 = c1.reindex(c2.index)

y = np.arange(len(c2)); h = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.2))
ax.barh(y + h/2, c1.values, h, color=OLD, label="v1, 3 okrugs")
ax.barh(y - h/2, c2.values, h, color=ACCENT, label="v2 export")
for yy, v in zip(y + h/2, c1.values):
    ax.text(v, yy, f" {v:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=8)
for yy, v in zip(y - h/2, c2.values):
    ax.text(v, yy, f" {v:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(c2.index)
ax.set_xlim(0, 115); ax.set_xlabel("% of objects populated")
ax.set_title("Attribute completeness"); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

n_geocoded = int(v2["enrichment_comment"].fillna("").str.contains("Maps.co").sum())
```

Address coverage is now **100%** (98% before), because the pipeline back-fills
missing addresses through the Maps.co geocoder — the `Enrichment comment` field
records this for **`{python} f"{n_geocoded:,}"`** objects
(`{python} f"{n_geocoded/n_v2*100:.0f}"`%). Geocoded addresses are derived, not
observed, so they should not be used to *validate* an object's location.
Opening hours and phone coverage are broadly unchanged; *opening date* remains
unusable at **`{python} f"{v2['opening_date_orig'].notna().mean()*100:.1f}"`%**
and should be dropped downstream.

## Okrug distribution: the v1 defect is fixed {#sec-okrug}

```{python}
# | label: fig-okrug-fix
# | fig-cap: "Objects per okrug: the first export (grey) against the new export (blue). The first export placed 84% of the three okrugs' objects in Oktyabrsky and only 33 in Lomonosovsky."
d1c = v1_3["district_en"].value_counts().reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0)
d2c = v2["district_en"].value_counts().reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0)

y = np.arange(len(OKRUG_ORDER)); h = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.2))
ax.barh(y + h/2, d1c.values, h, color=OLD, label=f"v1, 3 okrugs (n={n_v1_3:,})")
ax.barh(y - h/2, d2c.values, h, color=ACCENT, label=f"v2 export (n={n_v2:,})")
for yy, v in zip(y + h/2, d1c.values):
    ax.text(v, yy, f" {int(v):,} ({v/n_v1_3*100:.0f}%)", va="center", fontsize=8)
for yy, v in zip(y - h/2, d2c.values):
    ax.text(v, yy, f" {int(v):,} ({v/n_v2*100:.0f}%)", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(OKRUG_ORDER)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects"); ax.set_title("Objects per okrug — before and after")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.margins(x=0.22)
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

This is the central improvement of the delivery. In the first export the three
okrugs split
**`{python} ' / '.join(f"{int(v):,}" for v in d1c.values)`** (Lomonosovsky,
an okrug of roughly 60,000 residents, held **33 objects**); the new export
splits them
**`{python} ' / '.join(f"{int(v):,}" for v in d2c.values)`**, which is
consistent both with the geography of the city and with the 2022 stage, where
Oktyabrsky and Lomonosovsky held comparable counts.
@sec-okrug-agreement shows that the assignment also agrees with 2022 on every matched
record. **District-level analysis is defensible again** — for these three
okrugs. The remaining five okrugs of Arkhangelsk are outside this export and
their attribution is still unverified.

```{python}
# | label: fig-map
# | fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of the new export, coloured by okrug, on an OpenStreetMap/CARTO basemap."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.0))
for color, d in zip(sns.color_palette("colorblind", len(OKRUG_ORDER)), OKRUG_ORDER):
    sub = v2[v2["district_en"] == d]
    ax.scatter(sub["longitude"], sub["latitude"], s=6, alpha=0.5,
               color=color, label=f"{d} ({len(sub):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude"); ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("Objects by okrug — new export")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.54)))
try:
    # Tiles are cached in data/tile_cache, so only the first render needs
    # internet access; offline we fall back to the plain scatter.
    import contextily as ctx
    tile_cache = RAW.parent / "tile_cache"
    tile_cache.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    ctx.set_cache_dir(str(tile_cache))
    ctx.add_basemap(ax, crs="EPSG:4326", source=ctx.providers.CartoDB.Positron,
                    attribution_size=5)
    ax.grid(visible=False)
except Exception:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7, markerscale=2, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

The three okrugs form a contiguous, compact block covering the city centre and
the southern approach — the same footprint the 2022 stage studied. Unlike the
first export, the colouring now follows visible spatial boundaries rather than
cutting arbitrarily across them.

## Recoding to the 2022 taxonomy

As in the first report, every object is recoded into the **2022 seven-class
health taxonomy** (`category_2022`) with an identical rule over `category_orig`,
`type_orig` and `name_orig`, so the two reports remain comparable.


**`{python} f"{in_scheme:,}"`** objects

## Health infrastructure vs. risk factors

```{python}
# | label: healthrisk-compute
t = v2["type_orig"].fillna("").astype(str).str.lower()
cat_s = v2["category_orig"].fillna("").astype(str)
blob = (cat_s.str.lower() + " | " + t + " | " + v2["name_orig"].fillna("").str.lower())

health_sub = {
    "Medical": v2["category_2022"].eq("Medical"),
    "Sport & recreation": v2["category_2022"].eq("Sport"),
}
risk_sub = {
    "Fast food": cat_s.eq("фастфуд") | _has(t, "фастфуд"),
    "Alcohol": v2["category_2022"].eq("Alcohol shops"),
    "Tobacco": v2["category_2022"].eq("Tobacco outlets"),
    "Bars / pubs": _has(t, "бар", "паб") & ~_has(t, "барбер"),
    "Hookah / nightlife": _has(blob, "кальян", "ночной клуб", "лаунж"),
}
hr = pd.DataFrame({
    "Group": ["Health-supporting"]*len(health_sub) + ["Risk factor"]*len(risk_sub),
    "Subgroup": list(health_sub) + list(risk_sub),
    "Objects": [int(m.sum()) for m in health_sub.values()]
               + [int(m.sum()) for m in risk_sub.values()],
})
health_mask = np.logical_or.reduce(list(health_sub.values()))
risk_mask = np.logical_or.reduce(list(risk_sub.values()))
n_health, n_risk = int(health_mask.sum()), int(risk_mask.sum())
```

The same transparent heuristic as the first report separates
**health-supporting** infrastructure from **risk factors**. The new export holds
**`{python} f"{n_health:,}"`** health-supporting and
**`{python} f"{n_risk:,}"`** risk-factor objects across the three okrugs.

```{python}
# | label: fig-healthrisk
# | fig-cap: "Health-supporting infrastructure (blue) vs. risk factors (orange)."
order = hr.sort_values("Objects")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
ax.barh(order["Subgroup"], order["Objects"],
        color=[ACCENT if g == "Health-supporting" else RISK for g in order["Group"]])
for y_, v in enumerate(order["Objects"]):
    ax.text(v, y_, f" {v:,}", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects")
ax.set_title("Health-supporting (blue) vs. risk factors (orange)")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.margins(x=0.12)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: tbl-healthrisk-district
# | tbl-cap: "Health-supporting vs. risk objects by okrug, with the health-to-risk ratio."
tmp = v2.copy()
tmp["is_health"], tmp["is_risk"] = health_mask, risk_mask
g = tmp.groupby("district_en").agg(Objects=("name_orig", "size"),
                                   Health=("is_health", "sum"),
                                   Risk=("is_risk", "sum"))
g["Health:Risk"] = (g["Health"] / g["Risk"].replace(0, np.nan)).round(2)
g["Risk per 100 objects"] = (g["Risk"] / g["Objects"] * 100).round(1)
g = g.reindex(OKRUG_ORDER)
gt = g.reset_index().rename(columns={"district_en": "Okrug"})
gt["Health:Risk"] = gt["Health:Risk"].map(lambda x: "—" if pd.isna(x) else f"{x:.2f}")
gt["Risk per 100 objects"] = gt["Risk per 100 objects"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.1f}")
Markdown(gt.to_markdown(index=False))
```

**This is the first table in the project that can be read at face value**, since
it rests on corrected okrug labels. The health-to-risk ratio is broadly similar
across the three okrugs, with Mayskaya Gorka — the smallest and most residential
— showing the most favourable balance.

# Part II — the 2022 ↔ 2026 record comparison {#sec-comparison}

## Method and parameters

The workbook matches each row of the **2022 document**
(`220603 Все объекты, 3 округа gps (1).xlsx`, `{python} f"{n_doc1:,}"` rows)
against the **new 2026 export** (`{python} f"{n_declared:,}"` rows) using
coordinates, name similarity, and address, and classifies the outcome as a firm
*match*, a *probable match* needing review, or *not found*.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-cmp-params
# | tbl-cap: "Comparison run parameters, as recorded in the workbook's Сводка sheet."
params = pd.DataFrame({
    "Parameter": ["Document 1 (2022 stage)", "Document 2 (2026 export)",
                  "Distance tolerance", "Name-similarity threshold",
                  "Probable-match mode", "GPS-correction mode"],
    "Value": [f"{n_doc1:,} rows", f"{n_declared:,} rows", f"{tol_m} m",
              f"{name_thr}", MODE_EN(SUMMARY["Режим вероятных совпадений"]),
              MODE_EN(SUMMARY["Режим исправления GPS"])],
})
Markdown(params.to_markdown(index=False))
```

Note that the 2022 document used here (`{python} f"{n_doc1:,}"` rows) is a
**larger, GPS-annotated variant** of the 2022 file kept in this repository
(`data/raw/objects_3_districts_2022.xlsx`, 1,753 rows). The difference is
concentrated in the risk classes — *Tobacco outlets* alone goes from 46 rows in
the repository copy to 483 here — so this comparison exercises the risk side of
the taxonomy far more heavily than the first report could.

## Match outcomes

```{python}
# | label: fig-match-funnel
# | fig-cap: "Outcome for each of the 2022 document's rows."
doc1["status_en"] = doc1["Статус сравнения"].map(STATUS_EN)
sc = doc1["status_en"].value_counts().reindex(STATUS_ORDER)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 2.6))

        color=[STATUS_COLOR[s] for s in sc.index[::-1]])
for y_, v in enumerate(sc.values[::-1]):

ax.set_xlabel("2022 rows"); ax.set_title("2022 rows re-found in the 2026 export")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.margins(x=0.20)

found = n_match + n_prob
```

**`{python} f"{found:,}"` of `{python} f"{n_doc1:,}"` 2022 objects
(`{python} f"{found/n_doc1*100:.1f}"`%) are re-found in the 2026 export**, but
only `{python} f"{n_match/n_doc1*100:.1f}"`% as firm matches; the remaining
`{python} f"{n_prob/n_doc1*100:.1f}"`% are *probable* and flagged for manual
review. Read strictly — counting only firm matches — the continuity between the
stages is **`{python} f"{n_match/n_doc1*100:.0f}"`%, not 94%.** The distinction
matters for any longitudinal claim.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-summary-csv
# | tbl-cap: "Per-okrug comparison summary, as shipped in итоги_сравнения_3_округа.csv."
summ = pd.read_csv(SUM_FILE, sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig")
summ.columns = ["Okrug", "Rows in 2022 doc", "Matches", "Probable",
                "Not found", "Found total", "Found, %"]
summ["Okrug"] = summ["Okrug"].map(DISTRICT_EN).fillna(summ["Okrug"]).replace({"ВСЕГО": "TOTAL"})
summ["Found, %"] = summ["Found, %"].map("{:.1f}".format)
Markdown(summ.to_markdown(index=False))
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-match-by-cat
# | fig-cap: "Match outcome by 2022 category — the risk classes fare worst."
doc1["cat_en"] = doc1["Категория"].map(CATEGORY_EN).fillna(doc1["Категория"])
ctc = pd.crosstab(doc1["cat_en"], doc1["status_en"]).reindex(columns=STATUS_ORDER).fillna(0)
ctc = ctc.loc[ctc.sum(axis=1).sort_values().index]
pct = ctc.div(ctc.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
left = np.zeros(len(ctc))
for s in STATUS_ORDER:
    ax.barh(ctc.index, pct[s], left=left, color=STATUS_COLOR[s], label=s)
    left += pct[s].values
for y_, (idx, row) in enumerate(ctc.iterrows()):
    ax.text(101, y_, f" n={int(row.sum()):,}", va="center", fontsize=7, color="#444")
ax.set_xlim(0, 118); ax.set_xlabel("% of the category's 2022 rows")

ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right", ncol=3)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

The pattern is systematic and important for the project:

- **Medical organizations** re-find best — `{python} f"{pct.loc['Medical organizations', 'Match']:.0f}"`%
  firm matches. Clinics and pharmacies are well described in OSM.
- **Tobacco outlets** are the worst case: only
  `{python} f"{pct.loc['Tobacco outlets', 'Match']:.0f}"`% firm matches against
  `{python} f"{pct.loc['Tobacco outlets', 'Probable match']:.0f}"`% probable.
  The reason is taxonomic, not spatial — see @sec-drift.
- **Sport facilities** have the highest outright loss rate
  (`{python} f"{pct.loc['Sport facilities', 'Not found']:.0f}"`% not found):
  playgrounds, courts and school stadiums are exactly the objects OSM covers
  inconsistently.

```{python}
# | label: fig-match-quality
# | fig-cap: "Match geometry and name agreement. Firm matches cluster at zero distance and full name identity; probable matches are spatially close but nominally different."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.4, 3.0))
bins_d = np.linspace(0, 100, 41)
axes[0].hist(matches["Расстояние совпадения, м"].dropna(), bins=bins_d,
             color=ACCENT, alpha=0.85, label="Match")
axes[0].hist(probable["Расстояние совпадения, м"].dropna(), bins=bins_d,
             color=RISK, alpha=0.6, label="Probable")
axes[0].set_xlabel("Match distance, m"); axes[0].set_ylabel("Rows")
axes[0].set_title("Distance"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=7)

bins_s = np.linspace(0, 1, 21)
axes[1].hist(matches["Похожесть названия"], bins=bins_s, color=ACCENT,
             alpha=0.85, label="Match")
axes[1].hist(probable["Похожесть названия"], bins=bins_s, color=RISK,
             alpha=0.6, label="Probable")
axes[1].set_xlabel("Name similarity"); axes[1].set_title("Name agreement")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Median match distance is
**`{python} f"{matches['Расстояние совпадения, м'].median():.1f}"` m** for firm
matches and
**`{python} f"{probable['Расстояние совпадения, м'].median():.1f}"` m** for
probable ones — both well inside the `{python} f"{tol_m}"` m tolerance. What
separates the two groups is the *name*: median similarity
**`{python} f"{matches['Похожесть названия'].median():.2f}"`** vs.
**`{python} f"{probable['Похожесть названия'].median():.2f}"`**. Probable matches
are therefore mostly *the right building, an uncertain tenant* — a review task
that can be prioritised by name similarity.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-methods
# | tbl-cap: "Evidence used to establish each firm match (top methods)."
METHOD_EN = {
    "координаты": "coordinates", "точное название": "exact name",
    "близкая точка": "nearby point", "вероятная близкая точка": "probable nearby point",
    "точный адрес": "exact address",
    "объект уже сопоставлен с другой строкой": "object already matched to another row",
}


def method_en(s):
    for ru, en in METHOD_EN.items():
        s = s.replace(ru, en)
    return s


mm = matches["Способ совпадения"].value_counts().head(6).rename_axis("Method").reset_index(name="Rows")
mm["Method"] = mm["Method"].map(method_en)
mm["% of matches"] = (mm["Rows"] / n_match * 100).round(1)
mm["% of matches"] = mm["% of matches"].map("{:.1f}".format)
Markdown(mm.to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Okrug agreement between the stages {#sec-okrug-agreement}

```{python}
# | label: tbl-okrug-agreement
# | tbl-cap: "Okrug assigned in 2022 (rows) vs. okrug assigned by the 2026 export (columns), firm matches only."
oa = pd.crosstab(matches["Документ 1: Округ/район"].map(DISTRICT_EN),
                 matches["Документ 2: Округ/район"].map(DISTRICT_EN))
oa = oa.reindex(index=OKRUG_ORDER, columns=OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0).astype(int)
agree = int(np.trace(oa.values)); tot_oa = int(oa.values.sum())
oa.index.name = "2022 okrug"; oa.columns.name = None
Markdown(oa.reset_index().to_markdown(index=False))
```

The cross-tabulation is **perfectly diagonal**: all
`{python} f"{agree:,}"` of `{python} f"{tot_oa:,}"` firmly matched objects
(`{python} f"{agree/tot_oa*100:.0f}"`%) receive the same okrug in 2026 as they
had in 2022. This is independent confirmation that the okrug-assignment step now
works, and it is the strongest single piece of evidence in this delivery.

## Category drift between the stages {#sec-drift}

```{python}
# | label: fig-drift
# | fig-cap: "2022 category (rows) vs. 2026 export category (columns) for firmly matched objects. Off-diagonal mass shows where the new generic taxonomy dissolves the 2022 health classes."
dr = pd.crosstab(matches["Документ 1: Категория"].map(CATEGORY_EN),
                 matches["Документ 2: Категория"].map(CATEGORY_EN))
keep = dr.sum(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:8]
dr = dr[keep]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 3.6))
sns.heatmap(dr, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues", linewidths=0.5,
            linecolor="white", cbar_kws={"label": "objects"}, ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("2026 export category"); ax.set_ylabel("2022 category")
ax.set_title("Category drift, firmly matched objects")
plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha="right"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

same_cat = (matches["Документ 1: Категория"] == matches["Документ 2: Категория"]).mean()
tob_2022 = int((doc1["Категория"] == "Точки продажи табака").sum())
tob_2026 = int((v2["category_orig"] == "Точки продажи табака").sum())
alc_2022 = int((doc1["Категория"] == "Спецмагазины алкоголя").sum())
```

Only **`{python} f"{same_cat*100:.0f}"`%** of firmly matched objects keep the
same category label across the stages. The drift is not random — it is the
**collapse of the 2022 risk taxonomy into the generic 2026 scheme**:

- The 2022 document holds **`{python} f"{tob_2022:,}"` tobacco outlets**; the
  entire 2026 3-okrug export holds **`{python} f"{tob_2026}"`**. Matched 2022
  tobacco outlets land overwhelmingly in the generic *Shops* category, because
  the new export classifies the premises (a convenience store) rather than the
  product sold there.
- The same happens to the **`{python} f"{alc_2022:,}"` alcohol shops**: most
  matched rows come back as *Shops*.

This is a **classification change, not a change in the city**, and it is the
reason the project needs the derived `category_2022` recoding. It also sets a
hard limit: risk-factor objects that the 2022 stage identified by *what is sold*
cannot be recovered from the 2026 export by category alone, only by the
name/type heuristic — which will under-count.

## What each stage holds alone

```{python}
# | label: fig-only1
# | fig-cap: "The 130 objects present in 2022 but not re-found in 2026, by category."
o1c = only1["Документ 1: Категория"].map(CATEGORY_EN).value_counts()
barh(o1c, f"Only in the 2022 document (n={n_only1})", "Objects",
     color=RISK, figsize=(7.2, 3.0))
```

```{python}

# | fig-cap: "The 3,663 objects present in the 2026 export but absent from the 2022 document, by category."
o2c = only2["Документ 2: Категория"].map(CATEGORY_EN).value_counts()
barh(o2c, f"Only in the 2026 export (n={n_only2:,})", "Objects",
     figsize=(7.2, max(3.4, 0.32*len(o2c) + 1.2)))
```

The asymmetry is expected and mostly benign: the 2022 document was a
**purpose-built health inventory** of seven classes, whereas the 2026 export is
a **general city inventory**. Of the `{python} f"{n_only2:,}"` objects new in
2026, the large majority are *Shops*, *Organizations* and *Services* that the
2022 study never set out to collect. The
`{python} f"{n_only1}"` objects lost in the other direction are the material
finding: **`{python} f"{int(o1c.get('Sport facilities', 0))}"` of them are sport
facilities** — over a third — confirming the coverage gap seen in
@fig-match-by-cat.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-gps
# | tbl-cap: "GPS anomalies detected during the comparison."
gw = gps_warn.copy()
gw["Округ/район"] = gw["Округ/район"].map(DISTRICT_EN).fillna(gw["Округ/район"])
gw = gw[["Документ", "Строка", "Организация", "Округ/район", "Адрес",
         "Широта", "Долгота", "Расстояние от центра группы, м"]]
gw.columns = ["Document", "Row", "Name", "Okrug", "Address", "Lat", "Lon",
              "Distance from cluster centre, m"]
for c, f in [("Lat", "{:.4f}"), ("Lon", "{:.4f}"),
             ("Distance from cluster centre, m", "{:,.0f}")]:
    gw[c] = gw[c].map(f.format)
Markdown(gw.to_markdown(index=False))
```

The GPS-outlier check flagged **`{python} f"{len(gps_warn)}"` rows, both in the
2022 document** and none in the 2026 export — coordinates ~1,000-2,300 km from
the Arkhangelsk cluster centre (one lands near Kazan). One was auto-corrected
from its matched 2026 counterpart; the other could not be, because it was not
re-found. Two bad rows in 2,293 is a good result, but it confirms the 2022 file
needs a coordinate-sanity pass before any spatial reuse.

```{python}
    "Болезни системы кровообращения": "Circulatory disease",

    "Ожидаемая продолжительность жизни": "Life expectancy",
    "Болезни органов дыхания": "Respiratory disease",
    "Транспортная доступность": "Transport accessibility",
    "Средняя температура": "Mean temperature",
    "Дни экстремального холода": "Extreme cold days",
    "Максимальная температура": "Max temperature",
    "Минимальная температура": "Min temperature", "Осадки": "Precipitation",
    "Количество коек": "Hospital beds", "Количество врачей": "Doctors",
    "Количество больниц": "Hospitals", "Загрязнение воздуха": "Air pollution index",
    "Выбросы загрязняющих веществ": "Total emissions",
    "Качество воды": "Water quality index", "Средняя зарплата": "Average salary",
    "Обеспеченность жильем": "Living space per capita",
    "Уровень бедности": "Poverty rate", "Безработица": "Unemployment rate",
}
UNIT_EN = {"дней": "days", "чел.": "people", "на 1000 чел.": "per 1,000",
           "мм": "mm", "лет": "years", "индекс": "index", "ед.": "units",
           "тыс. т": "kt", "руб.": "RUB", "кв.м/чел.": "m²/person",
           "чел./кв.км": "people/km²", "°C": "°C", "%": "%"}

ind["section_en"] = ind["Раздел"].map(SECTION_EN).fillna(ind["Раздел"])
ind["indicator_en"] = ind["Показатель"].map(INDICATOR_EN).fillna(ind["Показатель"])
ind["unit_en"] = ind["Ед. изм."].map(UNIT_EN).fillna(ind["Ед. изм."])

n_ind = ind["Код показателя"].nunique()
years = sorted(ind["Год"].unique())
```

## Structure

A separate artefact from the object export: a **panel of
`{python} f"{n_ind}"` municipal indicators for Arkhangelsk across
`{python} f"{len(years)}"` years (`{python} f"{years[0]}-{years[-1]}"`)** —
`{python} f"{len(ind):,}"` observations in total — grouped into
`{python} f"{ind['Раздел'].nunique()}"` sections, plus a composite risk index.
It carries no object-level or okrug-level detail; it describes the city as a
whole.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-arktmed-sections
# | tbl-cap: "Indicator panel by section, with the sources cited for each."
sec = (ind.groupby("section_en")
          .agg(Indicators=("Код показателя", "nunique"),
               Observations=("Значение", "size"),
               Sources=("Источник", lambda s: ", ".join(
                   sorted({u.replace("https://", "").replace("http://", "").strip("/").split("/")[0]
                           for u in s}))))
          .sort_values("Indicators", ascending=False)
          .reset_index().rename(columns={"section_en": "Section"}))
Markdown(sec.to_markdown(index=False))
```

Every one of the `{python} f"{len(ind):,}"` rows is stamped
`Качество, % = 100`, and the `Месяц` column is entirely empty — the panel is
annual, with each year dated to 1 December.

## The composite risk index

```{python}
# | label: fig-risk
# | fig-cap: "Composite risk index for Arkhangelsk and its five components. Higher = greater risk."
RISK_COMP_EN = {"Демография": "Demography", "Экономика": "Economy",
                "Здоровье": "Health", "Климат": "Climate", "Экология": "Ecology"}
ri = risk_idx.copy()
ri["Год"] = pd.to_datetime(ri["Дата"]).dt.year

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.0))
for ru, en in RISK_COMP_EN.items():
    ax.plot(ri["Год"], ri[ru], marker="o", ms=4, lw=1.4, alpha=0.85, label=en)
ax.plot(ri["Год"], ri["Индекс риска"], marker="s", ms=6, lw=2.6, color="black",
        label="Composite index")
ax.set_xlabel("Year"); ax.set_ylabel("Risk score")
ax.set_title("Risk index and components, 2021-2026")
ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=3, loc="lower left")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

ri0, ri1 = ri["Индекс риска"].iloc[0], ri["Индекс риска"].iloc[-1]
```

The composite index falls from **`{python} f"{ri0:.2f}"`** (2021) to
**`{python} f"{ri1:.2f}"`** (2026), yet the verdict stays
*«повышенный риск»* — **elevated risk** — in all six years. The components pull
in opposite directions, which is the interesting part:

- **Economy** improves most (`{python} f"{ri['Экономика'].iloc[0]:.1f}"` →
  `{python} f"{ri['Экономика'].iloc[-1]:.1f}"`), driven by a 45% rise in nominal
  average salary. This is **not inflation-adjusted**, so the improvement is
  largely nominal and should not be read as a real gain.
- **Demography deteriorates** (`{python} f"{ri['Демография'].iloc[0]:.1f}"` →
  `{python} f"{ri['Демография'].iloc[-1]:.1f}"`) — the only component that gets
  worse. Total population falls by
  `{python} f"{(1 - ind.query('Показатель == \"Численность населения\"')['Значение'].iloc[-1] / ind.query('Показатель == \"Численность населения\"')['Значение'].iloc[0])*100:.1f}"`%
  while the 65+ group grows by
  `{python} f"{(ind.query('Показатель == \"Население 65+\"')['Значение'].iloc[-1] / ind.query('Показатель == \"Население 65+\"')['Значение'].iloc[0] - 1)*100:.1f}"`%.
- **Ecology** improves steadily; **Climate** barely moves.

Ageing against a shrinking base is precisely the demand-side driver for the
health-supporting infrastructure this project maps.

## Indicator trajectories

```{python}
# | label: fig-indicators
# | fig-cap: "All 28 indicators, indexed to 2021 = 100 so trajectories are comparable across units. Each series is scaled by the *absolute* 2021 value, so indicators that start negative (net migration, minimum temperature) still read upwards when they improve. Panels are grouped by section."
sections = ["Demography", "Health", "Healthcare", "Economy", "Ecology",
            "Climate", "Infrastructure"]
sections = [s for s in sections if s in set(ind["section_en"])]
ncol = 3
nrow = int(np.ceil(len(sections) / ncol))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrow, ncol, figsize=(7.4, 2.3*nrow), sharex=True)
axes = np.atleast_1d(axes).ravel()

for ax, s in zip(axes, sections):
    sub = ind[ind["section_en"] == s]
    for name, gsub in sub.groupby("indicator_en"):
        gsub = gsub.sort_values("Год")
        base = gsub["Значение"].iloc[0]
        # Scale by the ABSOLUTE 2021 value, not the signed one: net migration
        # and minimum temperature start negative, and plain division would
        # flip the direction of their trend.
        vals = ((gsub["Значение"] - base) / abs(base) * 100 + 100
                if base != 0 else gsub["Значение"])
        ax.plot(gsub["Год"], vals, marker="o", ms=2.5, lw=1.2, label=name)
    ax.axhline(100, color="#999", lw=0.8, ls="--")
    ax.set_title(s, fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
    ax.legend(fontsize=5.5, loc="best", frameon=False)
for ax in axes[len(sections):]:
    ax.set_visible(False)
fig.supylabel("Index, 2021 = 100", fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: tbl-indicators
# | tbl-cap: "Every indicator: first and last value, total change, and whether the series is exactly linear in time."
rows = []
for (s, name, unit), gsub in ind.groupby(["section_en", "indicator_en", "unit_en"]):
    gsub = gsub.sort_values("Год")
    v = gsub["Значение"].to_numpy()
    d2 = np.abs(np.diff(v, 2)).max() if len(v) > 2 else 0.0
    scale = max(abs(v).max(), 1e-9)
    rows.append({
        "Section": s, "Indicator": name, "Unit": unit,
        "2021": v[0], "2026": v[-1],
        "Change, %": (v[-1]/v[0] - 1) * 100 if v[0] != 0 else np.nan,
        "Linear": "yes" if d2 / scale < 1e-6 else "no",
    })
tab = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["Section", "Indicator"])
tab["2021"] = tab["2021"].map(lambda x: f"{x:,.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip("."))
tab["2026"] = tab["2026"].map(lambda x: f"{x:,.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip("."))
tab["Change, %"] = tab["Change, %"].map(lambda x: "—" if pd.isna(x) else f"{x:+.1f}")
Markdown(tab.to_markdown(index=False))

n_linear = int((tab["Linear"] == "yes").sum())
```

## The panel is modelled, not observed {#sec-arktmed-caveat}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not use these values as measurements
**`{python} f"{n_linear}"` of the `{python} f"{n_ind}"` indicators are exactly
linear in time** — the second difference of the series is zero to floating-point
precision. Real demographic, climatic and epidemiological series are never
exactly linear over six years.
:::

The evidence that the panel is generated rather than collected is direct:

1. **Exact linearity.** Mean temperature runs 1.60, 1.72, 1.84, 1.96, 2.08, 2.20
   °C — a perfect +0.12 °C per year. Emissions fall by exactly 3.5 kt each year.
   Only *Population 65+* deviates at all, and only slightly.
2. **The risk index is linear too**, in every component, which follows
   mechanically from the inputs.
3. **Two of the six years are in the future.** The panel runs to 2026 and is
   dated 2026-08-24, so the 2026 values — and arguably 2025 — are projections,
   yet they are stamped `Качество, % = 100` like everything else.
4. **Fractional people.** Population 0-14 is 59,672.371 in 2021; a census count
   cannot have a fractional part. The age bands are apportioned from a total,
   not counted.
5. **Sources are cited at domain level only** (`rosstat.gov.ru`,
   `minzdrav29.ru`, `fedstat.ru`, `open-meteo.com`, `rpn.gov.ru`,
   `dvinaland.ru`) with no table, dataset or retrieval date, so no value can be
   traced back to its origin.

The `Качество, % = 100` flag therefore describes **completeness of the generated
table, not fidelity to a source.** The panel is usable as a *structural template*
— it shows which indicators the ARKTMED system intends to deliver and in what
shape — but **no number in it should enter an analysis or a publication until
each series is re-sourced against the cited primary datasets.** The anchor year
2021 is the most likely to be genuine and is where verification should start.

# Key findings

1. **The okrug defect is fixed.** The new export splits the three okrugs
   `{python} ' / '.join(f"{int(v):,}" for v in d2c.values)` instead of the first
   export's `{python} ' / '.join(f"{int(v):,}" for v in d1c.values)`, and agrees
   with the 2022 stage on **100%** of firmly matched records. District-level
   analysis is defensible again for these three okrugs.
2. **Source diversity was lost in the process.** All
   `{python} f"{n_v2:,}"` objects are OSM-only; the 2GIS provider is absent, so
   **nothing in this delivery is independently corroborated** and counts are
   lower bounds.
3. **Continuity with 2022 is `{python} f"{n_match/n_doc1*100:.0f}"`%, not 94%.**
   `{python} f"{found/n_doc1*100:.1f}"`% of 2022 objects are re-found, but
   `{python} f"{n_prob/n_doc1*100:.0f}"`% only as *probable* matches awaiting
   review. Probable matches are usually the right building with an uncertain
   tenant, so they can be triaged by name similarity.
4. **The 2022 risk taxonomy does not survive the new category scheme.** Only
   `{python} f"{same_cat*100:.0f}"`% of matched objects keep their category;
   `{python} f"{tob_2022:,}"` tobacco outlets in 2022 correspond to
   `{python} f"{tob_2026}"` so-labelled objects in the 2026 export. Risk objects
   must be recovered through the `category_2022` heuristic, which under-counts.
5. **Sport facilities are the real coverage gap** —
   `{python} f"{pct.loc['Sport facilities', 'Not found']:.0f}"`% not found, and
   `{python} f"{int(o1c.get('Sport facilities', 0))}"` of the
   `{python} f"{n_only1}"` objects lost since 2022.
6. **The health-to-risk ratio is now computable per okrug** on trustworthy
   labels — the first substantive project output this data supports.
7. **The ARKTMED panel is synthetic.** `{python} f"{n_linear}"`/`{python} f"{n_ind}"`
   series are exactly linear and two of six years are in the future; treat it as
   a schema, not as data.

## Recommended next steps

- **Restore the 2GIS (and ideally Yandex) provider** and re-run the export;
  single-source data cannot support the 2022 methodology.
- **Extend the corrected export to all eight okrugs.** The fix is demonstrated
  on three; the other five remain unvalidated.
- **Triage the `{python} f"{n_prob:,}"` probable matches** in descending name
  similarity — the workbook already ranks them — to convert them to firm matches
  or rejections.
- **Freeze and validate `category_2022`** against the 2022 definitions,
  measuring specifically how many of the `{python} f"{tob_2022:,}"` tobacco and
  `{python} f"{alc_2022:,}"` alcohol objects it recovers.
- **Re-source the ARKTMED panel** indicator by indicator against Rosstat,
  Minzdrav29 and RPN, starting from 2021, before any of it is cited.
- **Audit the 2022 file's coordinates** — two rows are ~1,000 km off — and
  reconcile the 1,753-row repository copy with the 2,293-row variant used here.

# Appendix C — full recoding map to the 2022 taxonomy {.appendix}

Every combination of source category, source type and assigned 2022 class
present in the new export, with object counts — including everything that ended
up in *Other*. Because the rules also inspect object names, one category/type
pair can split across several classes; each split is a separate row. "—" marks
objects with no type recorded.

The table also makes the **rules' false positives visible**, which is why it is
printed in full. The *Industrial* class in particular over-reaches: it catches a
laundry, a hostel and a cosmetics shop whose *names* contain "фабрика" or
"завод", none of which is an industrial object. Each such row is a
single object and the effect on the totals is negligible, but it is concrete
evidence for the recommendation to freeze and validate `category_2022` against
the 2022 definitions rather than inherit it unchanged.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recode-map
# | tbl-cap: "Full recoding map for the new export: source category + source type → 2022 class."
sup = (v2.assign(type_orig=v2["type_orig"].fillna("—"),
                 category_orig=v2["category_orig"].fillna("—"))
         .groupby(["category_2022", "category_orig", "type_orig"], observed=True)
         .size().rename("Objects").reset_index())
sup["category_2022"] = pd.Categorical(sup["category_2022"], ORDER_2022, ordered=True)
sup = sup.sort_values(["category_2022", "Objects", "type_orig"],
                      ascending=[True, False, True])
sup["category_orig"] = sup["category_orig"].map(CATEGORY_EN).fillna(sup["category_orig"])
sup = sup.rename(columns={"category_2022": "2022 class",
                          "category_orig": "Source category",
                          "type_orig": "Source type (Russian)"})
Markdown(sup.to_markdown(index=False))
```
